items.name: Buildplate
items.signature: Buildplate(temp: int | None = None, wait: bool | None = False)
items.doc: This class represents a build plate used in 3D printing.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.Buildplate(temp=60, wait=False))

items.name: Extruder
items.signature: Extruder(on: bool | None = None, units: str | None = None, dia_feed: float | None = None, relative_gcode: bool | None = None, volume_to_e: float | None = None, total_volume: float | None = None, total_volume_ref: float | None = None, travel_format: str | None = None)
items.doc: Represents an extruder in a 3D printer.

items.name: ExtrusionGeometry
items.signature: ExtrusionGeometry(area_model: str | None = None, width: float | None = None, height: float | None = None, diameter: float | None = None, area: float | None = None)

items.name: Fan

items.doc: This class represents a generic fan component
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.Fan(speed_percent=100))

items.name: GcodeComment
items.signature: GcodeComment(text: str | None = None, end_of_previous_line_text: str | None = None)

items.name: GcodeControls
items.signature: GcodeControls(printer_name: str | None = None, initialization_data: dict | None = {}, save_as: str | None = None, include_date: bool | None = True)
items.doc: Control to adjust the style and initialization of the gcode.
items.snippet: gcode = fc.transform(steps, "gcode", fc.GcodeControls(printer_name="generic"))

items.name: Hotend
items.signature: Hotend(temp: int | None = None, wait: bool | None = False, tool: int | None = None)
items.doc: A class representing a generic hotend.

items.name: ManualGcode

items.doc: Custom Gcode class that allows adding a new line of Gcode defined by the 'text' attribute.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.ManualGcode(text="M400 ; wait for moves"))

items.name: PlotAnnotation
items.signature: PlotAnnotation(point: Point | None = None, label: str | None = None)
items.doc: Represents an annotation for a plot.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.PlotAnnotation(point=fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), label="Start"))

items.name: PlotControls
items.signature: PlotControls(color_type: str | None = 'z_gradient', line_width: float | None = None, style: str | None = None, tube_type: str | None = 'flow', tube_sides: int | None = 4, zoom: float | None = 1, hide_annotations: bool | None = False, hide_travel: bool | None = False, hide_axes: bool | None = False, neat_for_publishing: bool | None = False, raw_data: bool | None = False, return_fig: bool | None = False, printer_name: str | None = 'generic', initialization_data: dict | None = {})
items.doc: Control class to adjust the style of the plot.
items.snippet: fc.transform(steps, "plot", fc.PlotControls(color_type="z_gradient"))

items.name: Point
items.signature: Point(x: float | None = None, y: float | None = None, z: float | None = None, color: list | None = None)
items.doc: Represents the x, y, z position of the nozzle.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2))

items.name: Printer
items.signature: Printer(print_speed: float | None = None, travel_speed: float | None = None, command_list: dict | None = None, new_command: dict | None = None, speed_changed: bool | None = None, always_print_F: bool | None = None, always_print_xyz: bool | None = None)
items.doc: A class that represents a 3D printer.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.Printer(print_speed=1800, travel_speed=6000))

items.name: PrinterCommand
items.signature: PrinterCommand(id: str | None = None)
items.doc: Represents a command to be executed by a printer.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.PrinterCommand(id="home"))

items.name: StationaryExtrusion
items.signature: StationaryExtrusion(volume: float, speed: int)
items.doc: Represents stationary extrusion in a 3D printer.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.StationaryExtrusion(volume=15, speed=180))

items.name: circleXY
items.signature: circleXY(centre: Point, radius: float, start_angle: float, segments: int = 100, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY circle with the specified number of segments (defaulting to 100), centred about a Point, with the given radius, starting at the specified polar angle (radians), and with the z-position the same as that of the centre Point.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.circleXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), radius=20, start_angle=0, segments=64))

items.name: circleXY_3pt
items.signature: circleXY_3pt(pt1: Point, pt2: Point, pt3: Point, start_angle: float = None, start_at_first_point: bool = None, segments: int = 100, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY circle with the specified number of segments (defaulting to 100), defined by three points that the circle passes through. The start point in the returned list of points is defined by a polar angle (radians) or by setting start_at_first_point = True. The z-position is the same as that of pt1. Returns a list of Points.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.circleXY_3pt(fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 20, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2), segments=64))

items.name: ellipseXY
items.signature: ellipseXY(centre: Point, a: float, b: float, start_angle: float, segments: int = 100, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY ellipse with the specified number of segments (defaulting to 100), centred about a Point, with the given width (a) and height (b), starting at the specified polar angle (in radians), and with the z-position the same as that of the centre Point. Returns a list of Points representing the ellipse.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.ellipseXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), a=25, b=15, start_angle=0, segments=64))

items.name: helixZ
items.signature: helixZ(centre: Point, start_radius: float, end_radius: float, start_angle: float, n_turns: float, pitch_z: float, segments: int, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a helix in the Z direction with the specified number of segments and turns (partial turns permitted), centred about the Point centre, sized based on the start and end radius, starting at the specified polar angle (radians), defaulting to counter-clockwise.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.helixZ(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), start_radius=20, end_radius=20, start_angle=0, n_turns=10, pitch_z=0.25, segments=640))

items.name: polygonXY
items.signature: polygonXY(centre: Point, enclosing_radius: float, start_angle: float, sides: int, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY polygon with the specified number of sides, centered about a Point, sized based on the enclosing radius, starting at the specified polar angle (radians). The default direction is counter-clockwise.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.polygonXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), enclosing_radius=20, start_angle=0, sides=6))

items.name: rectangleXY
items.signature: rectangleXY(start_point: Point, x_size: float, y_size: float, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D XY rectangle starting and ending at a given Point (5 points returned), with specified size.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.rectangleXY(fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY - 20, z=0.2), x_size=40, y_size=40))

items.name: spiralXY
items.signature: spiralXY(centre: Point, start_radius: float, end_radius: float, start_angle: float, n_turns: float, segments: int, cw: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY spiral with the specified number of segments and turns (partial turns permitted), centred about a Point, defaulting to anti-clockwise.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.spiralXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), start_radius=5, end_radius=25, start_angle=0, n_turns=6, segments=240))

items.name: arcXY
items.signature: arcXY(centre: Point, radius: float, start_angle: float, arc_angle: float, segments: int = 100) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY arc with angles defined in radians and z-position the same as that of the centre point.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.arcXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), radius=20, start_angle=0, arc_angle=3.14159, segments=32))

items.name: arcXY_3pt
items.signature: arcXY_3pt(pt1: Point, pt2: Point, pt3: Point, segments: int = 100) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY arc passing through three specified points.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.arcXY_3pt(fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 15, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2), segments=32))

items.name: elliptical_arcXY
items.signature: elliptical_arcXY(centre: Point, a: float, b: float, start_angle: float, arc_angle: float, segments: int = 100) -> list
items.doc: Generate a 2D-XY elliptical arc with z-position the same as that of the centre point Args: centre (Point): The centre point of the arc. a (float): The x-width of the ellipse. b (float): The y-height of the ellipse. start_angle (float): The starting polar angle of the arc in radians. arc_angle (float): The angle of the arc in radians. segments (int, optional): The number of segments to divide the arc into. Defaults to 100.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.elliptical_arcXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), a=25, b=12, start_angle=0, arc_angle=3.14159, segments=48))

items.name: variable_arcXY
items.signature: variable_arcXY(centre: Point, start_radius: float, start_angle: float, arc_angle: float, segments: int = 100, radius_change: float = 0, z_change: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: Generate a arc with optionally varying radius and z-position. angles are defined in radians. z-position starts the same as that of the centre point and increased by z_change.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.variable_arcXY(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), start_radius=15, start_angle=0, arc_angle=3.14159, segments=48, radius_change=10, z_change=2.0))

items.name: sinewaveXYpolar
items.signature: sinewaveXYpolar(start_point: Point, direction_polar: float, amplitude: float, period_length: float, periods: int, segments_per_period: int = 16, extra_half_period: bool = False, phase_shift: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: Generate a sine wave with the set number of periods, starting at the start_point, with a given wave direction (polar angle in radians), given amplitude, with the distance between the midpoint of each line of the sine wave set by line_spacing. Optionally, an extra half period can be added and the wave can be phase-shifted.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.sinewaveXYpolar(fc.Point(x=CX - 30, y=CY, z=0.2), direction_polar=0, amplitude=4, period_length=10, periods=6, segments_per_period=16))

items.name: squarewaveXY
items.signature: squarewaveXY(start_point: Point, direction_vector: Vector, amplitude: float, line_spacing: float, periods: int, extra_half_period: bool = False, extra_end_line: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a square wave with the set number of periods, starting at the start_point, with a given wave direction (dictated by xy components of a Vector), given amplitude, with the distance between each line of the square wave set by line_spacing. Optionally, an extra half period and/or one extra line (top/bottom of square wave) can be added. Return a list of Points.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.squarewaveXY(fc.Point(x=CX - 30, y=CY, z=0.2), direction_vector=fc.Vector(x=1, y=0), amplitude=4, line_spacing=4, periods=5))

items.name: squarewaveXYpolar
items.signature: squarewaveXYpolar(start_point: Point, direction_polar: float, amplitude: float, line_spacing: float, periods: int, extra_half_period: bool = False, extra_end_line: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a squarewave with the set number of periods, starting at the start_point, with a given wave direction (polar angle in radians), given amplitude, with the distance between each line of the squarewave set by line_spacing. Optionally, an extra half period and/or one extra line (top/bottom of squrewave) can be added. Return a list of Points.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.squarewaveXYpolar(fc.Point(x=CX - 30, y=CY, z=0.2), direction_polar=0, amplitude=4, line_spacing=4, periods=5))

items.name: trianglewaveXYpolar
items.signature: trianglewaveXYpolar(start_point: Point, direction_polar: float, amplitude: float, tip_separation: float, periods: int, extra_half_period: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: Generate a triangle wave with the set number of periods, starting at the start_point, with a given wave direction (polar angle in radians), given amplitude, with the distance between neighbouring tips of the wave set by tip_separation. Optionally, an extra half period can be added. Return a list of Points.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.trianglewaveXYpolar(fc.Point(x=CX - 30, y=CY, z=0.2), direction_polar=0, amplitude=4, tip_separation=6, periods=6))

items.name: point_to_polar
items.signature: point_to_polar(target_point: Point, origin_point: Point) -> PolarPoint
items.doc: Convert a Cartesian point to polar coordinates. Find polar radius and angle (radians: 0 to 2pi) in XY plane of the given target point relative to a given origin Point.
items.snippet: pp = fc.point_to_polar(fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2))

items.name: polar_to_point
items.signature: polar_to_point(centre: Point, radius: float, angle: float) -> Point
items.doc: Convert polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates. Point XY coordinates of a point based on polar angle (radians) and radius from a centre point. The new Point has z = centre.z
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.polar_to_point(fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY, z=0.2), radius=20, angle=1.5708))

items.name: polar_to_vector
items.signature: polar_to_vector(length: float, angle: float) -> Vector
items.doc: Convert polar coordinates to a vector. Find an xy Vector based on an angle (radians) and length defined in polar coordinates.
items.snippet: vec = fc.polar_to_vector(length=10, angle=0.7854)

items.name: PolarPoint
items.signature: PolarPoint(radius: float, angle: float)
items.doc: Represents a point in polar coordinates.
items.snippet: pp = fc.PolarPoint(radius=20, angle=0.7854)

items.name: move
items.signature: move(geometry: Point | list, vector: Vector, copy: bool = False, copy_quantity: int = 2) -> Point | list
items.doc: Move 'geometry' (a Point or list of steps including Points) by 'vector'.
items.snippet: steps = fc.move(steps, fc.Vector(x=0, y=0, z=0.2), copy=True, copy_quantity=5)

items.name: move_polar
items.signature: move_polar(geometry: Point | list, centre: Point, radius: float, angle: float, copy: bool = False, copy_quantity: int = 2) -> Point | list
items.doc: Move 'geometry' (a Point or list of steps including Points) about a centre point by the given radius and angle (in radians) relative to the current radius and angle of each Point.
items.snippet: steps = fc.move_polar(steps, fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY), radius=0, angle=0.5236, copy=True, copy_quantity=6)

items.name: Vector
items.signature: Vector(x: float | None = None, y: float | None = None, z: float | None = None)
items.doc: A vector defined by x, y, and z distances.
items.snippet: vec = fc.Vector(x=0, y=0, z=0.2)

items.name: reflectXY
items.signature: reflectXY(p: Point, p1_reflect: Point, p2_reflect: Point) -> Point
items.doc: Reflects the x and y values of a Point about a line defined by two Points.
items.snippet: mirrored = fc.reflectXY(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=0), fc.Point(x=CX, y=100))

items.name: reflectXY_mc
items.signature: reflectXY_mc(p: Point, m_reflect: float, c_reflect: float) -> Point
items.doc: Reflects the x and y values of a Point about a line defined by m and c.
items.snippet: mirrored = fc.reflectXY_mc(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), m_reflect=1, c_reflect=0)

items.name: reflectXYpolar
items.signature: reflectXYpolar(p: Point, p_reflect: Point, angle_reflect: float) -> Point
items.doc: Reflects the x and y values of a point about a line defined by a point and polar angle (radians).
items.snippet: mirrored = fc.reflectXYpolar(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY), angle_reflect=1.5708)

items.name: ramp_polar
items.signature: ramp_polar(steplist: list, centre: Point, radius_change: float = 0, angle_change: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: Linearly changes the angle (radians) and radius of a list of Points about a given centre point.
items.snippet: steps = fc.ramp_polar(steps, fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY), radius_change=5.0, angle_change=0.0)

items.name: ramp_xyz
items.signature: ramp_xyz(steplist: list, x_change: float = 0, y_change: float = 0, z_change: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: Linearly increase x/y/z values of a list of Points by x_change/y_change/z_change.
items.snippet: steps = fc.ramp_xyz(steps, z_change=2.0)

items.name: segmented_line
items.signature: segmented_line(point1: Point, point2: Point, segments: int) -> list
items.doc: Return a list of Points linearly spaced between the start Point and end Point. The total number of Points in the list is segments+1.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.segmented_line(fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2), segments=20))

items.name: segmented_path
items.signature: segmented_path(points: list, segments: int) -> int
items.doc: Calculate a segmented path (equidistant points) based on a list of points and the desired number of segments.
items.snippet: steps = fc.segmented_path(steps, segments=50)

items.name: travel_to
items.signature: travel_to(geometry: Point | list) -> list
items.doc: Returns a list of objects to turn extrusion off, travel to a point, then turn extrusion on.
items.snippet: steps.extend(fc.travel_to(fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY + 20, z=0.2)))

items.name: angleXY_between_3_points
items.signature: angleXY_between_3_points(start_point: Point, mid_point: Point, end_point: Point) -> float
items.doc: Returns the angle from start_point to end_point, about mid_point.
items.snippet: ang = fc.angleXY_between_3_points(fc.Point(x=CX + 10, y=CY), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 10))

items.name: BoundingBox
items.signature: BoundingBox(minx: float | None = None, midx: float | None = None, maxx: float | None = None, rangex: float | None = None, miny: float | None = None, midy: float | None = None, maxy: float | None = None, rangey: float | None = None, minz: float | None = None, midz: float | None = None, maxz: float | None = None, rangez: float | None = None)
items.doc: Represents the geometric measures of a bounding box, including mid values and ranges.
items.snippet:
bb = fc.BoundingBox()
bb.calc_bounds(steps)

items.name: centreXY_3pt
items.signature: centreXY_3pt(pt1: Point, pt2: Point, pt3: Point) -> Point
items.doc: Calculate the centre point of a circle passing through three points.
items.snippet: c = fc.centreXY_3pt(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 10, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 10, y=CY, z=0.2))

items.name: distance
items.signature: distance(point1: Point, point2: Point) -> float
items.doc: Calculate the Euclidean distance between two points in 3D space.
items.snippet: d = fc.distance(fc.Point(x=0, y=0, z=0), fc.Point(x=10, y=0, z=0))

items.name: interpolated_point
items.signature: interpolated_point(point1: Point, point2: Point, interpolation_fraction: float) -> Point
items.doc: Return an interpolated point a fraction of the way from point1 to point2.
items.snippet: pt = fc.interpolated_point(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 10, y=CY, z=0.2), interpolation_fraction=0.25)

items.name: midpoint
items.signature: midpoint(point1: Point, point2: Point) -> Point
items.doc: Return the mid-point between two points.
items.snippet: mid = fc.midpoint(fc.Point(x=CX - 10, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 10, y=CY, z=0.2))

items.name: path_length
items.signature: path_length(points: list) -> float
items.doc: Calculates the total length of a path defined by a list of points.
items.snippet: print("Length:", fc.path_length(steps))

items.name: check
items.signature: check(steps: list)
items.doc: Check a list of steps and report what type of classes are included and whether the list is 2D. FullControl requires it to be 1D for processing.
items.snippet: fc.check(steps)

items.name: export_design
items.signature: export_design(steps: list, filename: str)
items.doc: Export design (list of steps) to a JSON file.
items.snippet: fc.export_design(steps, "my_design")

items.name: find_extruder_state
items.signature: find_extruder_state(steps)
items.doc: Finds final extruder state if any changes occur in steps. Can be used to find extruder state for use with first_print_point and last_print_point.
items.snippet: ext_on = fc.find_extruder_state(steps)

items.name: first_point
items.signature: first_point(steps: list, fully_defined: bool = True) -> Point
items.doc: Return the first Point in the list.
items.snippet: p0 = fc.first_point(steps)

items.name: first_print_point
items.signature: first_print_point(steps, extruder)
items.doc: Returns first point in steps where the extruder is on, the initial extruder state should be set.
items.snippet: p_start = fc.first_print_point(steps, extruder=fc.Extruder(on=True))

items.name: fix
items.signature: fix(steps: list, result_type: str, controls)
items.doc: Validate and normalize a list of steps (flattening nested lists and filling initial XYZ) before gcode or plot generation.
items.snippet: steps = fc.fix(steps, "gcode", fc.GcodeControls())

items.name: flatten
items.signature: flatten(steps: list) -> list
items.doc: Takes a list in which some elements are lists in the second dimension. Returns a flattened 1D list.
items.snippet: steps = fc.flatten(steps)

items.name: import_design
items.signature: import_design(fc_module_handle, filename: str)
items.doc: Import a previously exported design (list of steps).
items.snippet: steps = fc.import_design(fc, "my_design")

items.name: last_point
items.signature: last_point(steps: list, fully_defined: bool = True) -> Point
items.doc: Return the last Point in the list.
items.snippet: pn = fc.last_point(steps)

items.name: last_print_point
items.signature: last_print_point(steps, extruder)
items.doc: Returns last point in steps where the extruder is on, the initial extruder state should be set.
items.snippet: p_end = fc.last_print_point(steps, extruder=fc.Extruder(on=True))

items.name: linspace
items.signature: linspace(start: float, end: float, number_of_points: int) -> list
items.doc: Generate evenly spaced floats from start to end.
items.snippet: vals = fc.linspace(0.0, 10.0, 11)

items.name: points_only
items.signature: points_only(steps: list, track_xyz: bool = True) -> list
items.doc: Converts steps of Points and control to only Points and returns a new list.
items.snippet: pts = fc.points_only(steps, track_xyz=True)

items.name: relative_point
items.signature: relative_point(reference: Point | list, x_offset: float, y_offset: float, z_offset: float)
items.doc: Returns an fc.Point object with x, y, z positions relative to a reference point.
items.snippet: steps.append(fc.relative_point(steps, x_offset=10, y_offset=0, z_offset=0))

items.name: transform
items.signature: transform(steps: list, result_type: str, controls: GcodeControls | PlotControls = None, show_tips: bool = True)
items.doc: Transform a fullcontrol design (a list of class instances) into the specified result_type.
items.snippet: gcode = fc.transform(steps, "gcode", fc.GcodeControls(printer_name="generic"))

items.name: angleZ
items.signature: angleZ(start_point: Point, end_point: Point) -> float
items.doc: return the angle (radians) of a line down from the Z axis
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
az = fclab.angleZ(fc.Point(x=0, y=0, z=0), fc.Point(x=10, y=0, z=10))

items.name: arc_sinewaveXY
items.signature: arc_sinewaveXY(centre: Point, radius: float, amplitude: float, start_angle: float, arc_angle: float, periods: int, segments_per_period: int = 16, extra_half_period: bool = False, phase_shift: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: Generate a sine wave with the set number of periods, starting at the start_point, with a given wave direction (polar angle in radians), given amplitude, with the distance between the midpoint of each line of the sine wave set by line_spacing. Optionally, an extra half period can be added and the wave can be phase-shifted.

items.name: bezier
items.signature: bezier(control_points, num_points = 10, end_point = True)
items.doc: returns a bezier curve with num_points based on the supplied control points, ending on the final control point if end_point is True. returns list of points in curve
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps.extend(fclab.bezier([fc.Point(x=CX - 25, y=CY - 15, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 30, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 25, y=CY - 15, z=0.2)], num_points=40))

items.name: bezier_through_points
items.signature: bezier_through_points(control_points, num_points = 10, iteration_fraction = 0.5, iterations = 20)
items.doc: create a bezier curve that approximately passes through the control points. control points are iteratively moved to get the bezier curve to pass closer to each control point with each iteration. iteration fraction indicates how far to move the control points in each iteration, relative to the distance between the nearest point of the bezier curve to the control point.
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps.extend(fclab.bezier_through_points([fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 20, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2)], num_points=40))

import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps.extend(fclab.catmull_rom_spline([fc.Point(x=CX - 20, y=CY, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX, y=CY + 20, z=0.2), fc.Point(x=CX + 20, y=CY, z=0.2)], num_points=40, tension=0.5))

items.doc: adjust c rotation for a list of points to ensure all points are rotated (by c) to have the same polar angle in the XY plane relative to the centre point. Set initial_c (degreed) to adjust the desired initial orientation

items.name: convex_pathsXY
items.signature: convex_pathsXY(path1: list, path2: list, lines: int, vary_speed: bool = False, speed_ref: float = None, width_ref: float = None, travel: bool = True, zigzag: bool = False, overextrusion_percent: float = 0) -> list
items.doc: generate a series of paths to fill the space between supplied path1 and path2 with streamlined lines of continuously varying extrusion width. the points in each path are directly interpolated between. if vary_speed=True, the reference speed and extrusion width must be supplied, and the speed of the nozzle will continuously vary to maintain contant volumetric flowrate. if travel==True (default), there will be travel from the end of each path to the beginning of the next. set zigzag==True to alternate the printing direction of each path. set overextrusion_percent > 0 to overextrude to improve lateral bonding between paths. research study: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346098541
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps.extend(fclab.convex_pathsXY(path1, path2, lines=10))

items.doc: check if two lines cross within their length, one defined by Points a1,a2, the other by b1,b2. only x and y components are considered. return true if they cross

items.name: fill_base_full
items.signature: fill_base_full(steps: list, segments_per_layer: int, solid_layers: int, extrusion_width: float)
items.doc: see fill_base_simple for an explanation of how this work
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
base_steps = fclab.fill_base_full(steps, segments_per_layer=64, solid_layers=2, extrusion_width=0.45)

items.name: fill_base_simple
items.signature: fill_base_simple(steps: list, segments_per_layer: int, solid_layers: int, extrusion_width: float)
items.doc: take a vase_mode list of steps, calculate a convex fill for the first layer, which is identified based on the first (segments_per_layer+1) points. Then, for each layer, for the required number of solid layers, print the first layer's solid fill (outwards-in) using the convex function, then travel back to the last point of the layer. The first layer is copied because the convex function is computationally demanding, which is fine for parts where the first few layers are similar. If the outline is changing a lot over the first few layers, use fill_base_full instead, which finds the outline for each solid layer and used that to create the solid fill using the convex function for each new outline.
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
base_steps = fclab.fill_base_simple(steps, segments_per_layer=64, solid_layers=2, extrusion_width=0.45)

items.name: loop_between_lines
items.signature: loop_between_lines(point_a1: Point, point_a2: Point, point_b1: Point, point_b2: Point, extension: float, travel: bool = False, retract: bool = False, num_points: int = 10, linearity: int = 0) -> list
items.doc: move along a bezier curve to get from the end of one line to the beginning of the next line. first line defined by point_a1 and point_a2. second line defined by point_b1 and point_b2. bezier starts at point_a2, ends at point_b1, and has control points that are directly extended from lines a and b by the distance of the 'extension' parameter. 'linearity' (0 to 10) defines how close the loop gets to the control points (10 = directly through them). returns a list of fc.Points if travel=False, otherwise, returns a list of points and fc.Extruders to turn extrusion off at point_a2 and on at point_b1 (with retraction if retract=True).
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps.extend(fclab.loop_between_lines(p1, p2, p3, p4, extension=5.0))

items.name: offset_path
items.signature: offset_path(points: list, offset: float, flip: bool = False, repeats: int = 1, arc_outer_corners: bool = False, arc_segments: int = 8, travel: bool = False, include_original: bool = False) -> list
items.doc: return an offset path (list of Points) defined by the parameter 'points' and 'offset'. parameter 'flip' changes the direction of the offset. multiple offset paths can be generated by setting 'repeats' > 1. external corners can be given a radii by setting 'arc_outer_corners' as True. 'arc_segments' controls the number of segments for the newly created arcs. set 'travel' to True to travel to the first point in each offset path quickly without extruding, resulting in the returned list including Point and Extuder objects. 'include_original' can be used to include the original path as well as offset paths in the returned list.
items.snippet:
import lab.fullcontrol as fclab
steps = fclab.offset_path(steps, offset=0.8, repeats=2)

items.name: rotate
items.signature: rotate(geometry: Point | list, axis_start: Point, axis_end_or_direction: Point | str, angle_rad: float, copy: bool = False, copy_quantity: int = 2) -> Point | list
items.doc: rotate 'geometry' (a Point or list of steps including Points) about an axis by a defined angle (radians). the axis is defined by two points for the axis_start and axis_end or by one point for axis_start and a direction 'x', 'y' or 'z'. elements in a list that are not Points pass through and are replicated without modification. if copy==True, multiple copies of 'geometry' are created, each offset by 'vector' from the previous copy. 'copy_quantity' includes the position of the original geometry. return the new geometry as a list (original geometry is not edited).
